alpha_3a_review.required_claim:
Fix a coordinate orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ for the mirror convention. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere. A connected-sum datum consists of one smoothly embedded closed three-ball around a short subarc of $K$ and one around a short subarc of $J$, each meeting its knot in a single trivial properly embedded arc, together with the fixed standard orientation-reversing boundary identification of the two standard oriented ball boundaries that joins the oriented arcs into one circle. Choose this standard map once in the standard two-ball model so that it commutes with $r$ and an orientation-preserving half-turn interchanging the two balls preserves the joining convention. Here a trivial arc is an embedded interval in a ball that is carried by an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of ball-arc pairs to a straight diameter. Remove the interiors of the two balls and glue the remaining boundary spheres using this fixed identification; the resulting oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere is a connected sum of $K$ and $J$, denoted $K\#J$ for the specified datum.

The **standard unknot** is the oriented unit circle in a fixed coordinate two-plane of $S^3\subset\mathbb R^4$. A knot is **nontrivial** if it is not ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $S^3$ to the standard unknot. A nontrivial knot is **prime** if it has no connected-sum presentation whose two summand knots are both nontrivial.

Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $\nu(K)=TS^3|_K/TK$ be its quotient normal bundle. Equip $\nu(K)$ with a chosen smooth fibre norm $\|\cdot\|$. Let $\Phi:\Omega\to S^3$ be a tubular-neighbourhood map from an open neighbourhood $\Omega$ of the zero section in $\nu(K)$ that restricts to the inclusion of $K$. For $\epsilon>0$, define the closed disk subbundle
$$
D_\epsilon\nu(K):=\{v\in\nu(K):\|v\|\le\epsilon\}.

$$
E_K:=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}_{S^3}N(K).
$$
Retain its boundary $T_K:=\partial E_K=\partial N(K)$, orient $E_K$ by restriction of the fixed orientation of $S^3$, and orient $T_K$ as the boundary of $E_K$. The choice of tubular map and radius is part of the input to this definition.

alpha_3a_review.required_claim: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Identify the standard oriented three-sphere with $S^3=\{(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2:|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2=1\}$ and choose $0<r<1$. The standard unknotted Heegaard torus is $T_r=\{|z_1|=r,\ |z_2|=\sqrt{1-r^2}\}$; its two sides are solid tori. In the angular coordinates $(u,v)\in(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^2$ given by $(u,v)\mapsto(r e^{2\pi i u},\sqrt{1-r^2}e^{2\pi i v})$, let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the first and second coordinate classes in $H_1(T_r;\mathbb Z)$. For coprime nonzero integers $p,q$, the **oriented torus knot** $T(p,q)$ is the image of $s\mapsto(r e^{2\pi i p s},\sqrt{1-r^2}e^{2\pi i q s})$, for $s\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, oriented by increasing $s$; it represents the primitive slope $p\alpha+q\beta$. The mirror convention is the reflection $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(z_1,\overline{z_2})$, which sends $T(p,q)$ to $T(p,-q)$ with image orientation, and reversing the knot orientation gives $T(-p,-q)$. For nonzero $p,q$ with $d=\gcd(|p|,|q|)>1$, the corresponding torus link is the union of $d$ disjoint parallel copies of the primitive slope $(p/d,q/d)$; it is not a single embedded curve of class $p\alpha+q\beta$. The exterior is $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ for a chosen closed tubular neighborhood. A positive meridian is the oriented boundary of a normal disk, and a preferred longitude is a degree-one class on $\partial E_K$ whose image in $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ is zero; this definition alone asserts neither existence nor uniqueness.

alpha_3a_review.required_claim:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $p,q$ be coprime nonzero integers, let $K=T(p,q)$ be the oriented primitive slope curve in the standard Heegaard torus, and let $\rho_t(z_1,z_2)=(e^{2\pi i p t}z_1,e^{2\pi i q t}z_2)$ be the weighted circle action on the unit $S^3\subset\mathbb C^2$. Choose $N(K)$ to be a sufficiently small closed metric tube around the orbit $K$ for the round metric; this tube is invariant because $\rho_t$ is isometric and preserves $K$. Set $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$. Let $x$ and $y$ be based generators of the fundamental groups of the two solid-torus pieces obtained by cutting $E_K$ along the annulus left on the Heegaard torus, oriented so that the annulus core maps to $x^p$ and $y^q$. Then

$$\pi_1(E_K)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle.$$

The common element $h=x^p=y^q$ is central and represents a regular fiber of a Seifert fibration of $E_K$ over a disk. The fibration has two distinguished core fibers of multiplicities $|p|$ and $|q|$; a fiber of multiplicity one is regular, and a fiber of multiplicity greater than one is exceptional. Thus there are exactly two exceptional fibers when $|p|,|q|>1$, and one is regular when one absolute parameter is $1$.

For any integers $\alpha,\beta$ with $p\alpha+q\beta=1$, compatible based paths identify the positive normal-disk meridian and preferred longitude in the peripheral system as

$$\mu=y^\alpha x^\beta,\qquad \lambda=h\mu^{-pq}.$$

Here the positive meridian is the oriented boundary of a normal disk, and the preferred longitude has degree one around $K$ and maps to zero in $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$. Their homology classes form a basis of $H_1(\partial E_K;\mathbb Z)$, so both classes are primitive.

Suppose there is a continuous map $f:(D^2,\partial D^2)\to(M,F)$ whose boundary lies in the relative interior of $F$ and has class outside $N$. Then there is a properly embedded piecewise linear disk in $M$, with boundary in the relative interior of $F$, whose boundary class is outside $N$.

In particular, if a connected boundary component has noninjective induced fundamental-group map into $M$, it contains an essential simple closed curve bounding a properly embedded piecewise linear disk in $M$. Boundary classes outside $N$ are understood up to conjugation by a basepath in $F$.
